summary: Woodstock, NH fire tower on Grandview Mountain, built 1939 by the Forest Service and operated until 1948; torn down about 1960.

facts.status_note: Tower gone; the Forest Lookouts page lists it as removed. A 2012 blog post reported supports from the old tower still on the summit a few years earlier.

notes_for_editor: Dates for 1921, 1939, 1948 and about 1960 come from one 2012 blog post, which credits firelookout.org; the 1939 Herald and 1940 Groton Times items come via Forest Lookouts quotes. Conflict: the blog says the tower was torn down about 1960, yet its writer found supports still standing at the summit a few years before 2012; the story reports both. The hiking list entry is 'Grandview (East Peak)', 2000 ft, which may not be the same summit as the 2012-ft Grandview in the blog; matched by name and town, and the story says the list does not establish identity. Forest Service agency is from the blog only. Facebook posts (Upper Pemigewasset Historical Society; Instagram) describe a 1939 tower dismantled around 1960 but could not be read. A Laconia Daily Sun article on the 1939-1948 tower was rate-limited (429) and unread. Height kept as 40 ft in design, not converted to height_m because it is not stated as height to the cab floor. No photos found. Search budget: 2 WebSearch calls; about 5 page reads.
